# SMA-827: Gemini thought signatures round trip through a provider-data part in core

Linear: [SMA-827](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-827). Related: SMA-820 (merge of same-role
contents, tool-result boundary), SMA-565 (stale `gemini-2.5-flash` ids).

## Intent

Gemini 3 models put a `thoughtSignature` on the `functionCall` parts of a response. The next
request must send each signature back on the same part. If a call in the current turn has no
signature, the API returns HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall
parts". The SDK reads no signature and sends none. So every tool loop on Gemini 3 fails at the
second model call. For a new user, every available Gemini model is a Gemini 3 model (the 2.x ids
return HTTP 404), so the Gemini provider cannot run a tool loop at all.

Core has no place for provider data. Anthropic has the same gap: its stream drops
`signature_delta` (`providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:122`) and its request translator drops
`ContentPart::Reasoning` ("signature round-trip not yet supported"). Sven decided on 2026-11-20
that the new core shape must also hold Anthropic thinking signatures. This PR fixes Gemini only.

## Goals

1. Core gets one general carrier for opaque provider data, in the stream and in the history. The
   carrier can hold a Gemini signature on a tool call and, later, an Anthropic thinking signature
   or `redacted_thinking` block.
2. The Gemini stream translator keeps the `thoughtSignature` of each part.
3. The Gemini request translator sends each signature back on the same part.
4. A history with no signatures (a stored session, a history from another provider, a
   hand-built history) still works on Gemini 3.
5. The signature survives the session store, the durable runners and a handoff, because it lives
   in the item history.

## Non-goals

- The Anthropic round trip. A follow-up Linear ticket does it with the same carrier.
- OpenAI Responses `encrypted_content` reasoning items. The carrier can hold them later.
- Gemini thought summaries (`includeThoughts`, `thought: true` parts, translator item D3).
- Scripted evals (`evals/src/script.rs` `ScriptEvent`) cannot express the new event. No change.
- A new `AgentEvent` variant. Provider data stays inside `MessageOutput` items.
- SMA-565 (the stale model ids in the crate docs).

## Anti-goals

- A breaking change in core. Sven chose the additive approach (approach A).
- Provider data that reaches a provider it does not belong to. One provider's data must never be
  sent to another provider, and must never make another provider's request invalid.
- A change to the text that users see: the final output, the CLI output and the HTTP DTO `output`
  must not change because a tool-only turn now carries an `AssistantMessage`.

## Approaches

- **A. New additive variants (chosen by Sven on 2026-11-20).** Add `ModelEvent::ProviderData` and
  `ContentPart::ProviderData`. Both enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is not a breaking change,
  and core gets a patch bump. The data sits next to the call in the same `AssistantMessage`, not on
  the call. A tool-only turn now has an `AssistantMessage`, so some text consumers need a guard.
- **B. A new field on existing variants.** `provider_data` on `Item::ToolCall`,
  `ContentPart::ToolUse`, `ContentPart::Reasoning` and `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`. The data model
  is cleaner, but the variant fields are not `#[non_exhaustive]`: about 300 edits (130
  `Item::ToolCall` sites, 162 `ToolCallDelta` sites), broken user code, and a minor bump for core
  and every dependent. Rejected.
- **C. A signature cache in `GeminiModel` plus the dummy signature.** No core change, but the
  signatures do not survive a restart, a session store or a durable runner, and it does nothing
  for Anthropic. Rejected.

## Design

### Core types

```rust
// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs
ModelEvent::ProviderData {
    /// Stable name of the provider that owns `data`, for example "gemini".
    provider: String,
    /// The tool call that `data` belongs to, when it belongs to one.
    call_id: Option<String>,
    /// Opaque payload. Only the owning provider reads it.
    data: serde_json::Value,
}

// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/item.rs
ContentPart::ProviderData {
    provider: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    call_id: Option<String>,
    data: serde_json::Value,
}
```

Serde form: `{"type":"provider_data","provider":"gemini","call_id":"fc_0","data":{...}}`.
The rustdoc states the contract:

- A provider reads only the parts whose `provider` equals its own name, and ignores all others.
- A translator must not send a part of another provider, and must not fail because of one.
- The meaning of `call_id: Some(id)` is: the data belongs to the next tool call with that id after
  this `AssistantMessage` (call ids can repeat across turns, so the scope is the same turn).
- The meaning of `call_id: None` is: the data belongs to the message that holds the part. Its
  position in `content` is part of the meaning (Anthropic will put a signature immediately after its
  `Reasoning` part).

`ProviderData` is a public constant-like name per provider. The Gemini crate uses `"gemini"` for both
the Developer API and Vertex, as one `pub(crate) const PROVIDER: &str`.

### Core accumulator (`ModelTurnAccumulator`, `build_items`)

- `observe` keeps each `ModelEvent::ProviderData` in arrival order, in a new
  `provider_data: Vec<ContentPart>` field.
- `build_items` makes the `AssistantMessage` when text, reasoning **or** provider data is not empty.
  Content order: `Reasoning`, `Text`, then the `ProviderData` parts in arrival order.
- Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items after the message, in the existing `call_id`-sorted order.
- The rustdoc of `ModelTurn::items` changes to say the message can hold provider data only.

### Core: the other places that match on the new variants

- `token_counter.rs` `part_chars`: `ProviderData` counts as 0 characters. It is not model-visible
  text, and only the owning provider sends it. (My call: a Gemini signature can be some KB, but
  Google does not document it as billed input text. The builder can revisit this if a test shows it
  matters.)
- `agent.rs` event forwarding (around line 1475): `ModelEvent::ProviderData` is not forwarded as an
  `AgentEvent`. The accumulator still observes it.
- `agent.rs` injection allow-list (around line 1298) already rejects an unknown part. No change.

### Core and runtime: text consumers of `MessageOutput`

A tool-only turn now gives a `MessageOutput` event whose message has no `Text` part. The session
recorder needs this event (`session.rs:894`), so the event stays. Each consumer that reads text from
it must treat a message with no `Text` part as "no text", not as "empty text":

- `runner.rs` (around lines 434 and 513): clear and rebuild the final output only when the message
  holds at least one `Text` part. Today a ProviderData-only message would erase the earlier text,
  and a run that stops after a tool-only turn would lose its output.
- `workflow.rs` `assistant_text`: return `None` for a message with no `Text` part. Check its callers
  in `workflow.rs` and `graph.rs`.
- `cli/src/repl.rs` (around line 221): print the newline only when the message has text.
- `runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs` (around lines 366-390): a message with no `Text` part must
  not close an open text or tool-call span. The builder confirms the AG-UI event order with a test.
- `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` DTOs already skip an empty text. Add no code, but keep one test
  that proves a tool-only turn does not change `output`.

The builder searches the workspace for other code that takes text from `MessageOutput` or from an
`AssistantMessage` and applies the same rule.

### Other provider translators

Each translator already drops an unknown part with a wildcard arm. The risk is an
`AssistantMessage` that holds only foreign provider data:

- Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini and OpenAI Responses already send nothing for an empty message.
- OpenAI Chat and LiteLLM emit `{"role":"assistant","content":""}`. When `Item::ToolCall` items
  follow, they merge into that message, and the result is valid. Alone, it is an empty assistant
  message, which the API can reject. Change: an assistant message with no text and no tool calls is
  not emitted, and the following tool calls still form one assistant message. Add a test for both
  cases (ProviderData-only message alone; ProviderData-only message then two tool calls).

### Gemini stream translator (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)

- `sse.rs` `Part` gets `thought_signature: Option<String>` (`thoughtSignature` on the wire, a
  sibling of `functionCall` and `text` in the same part).
- For a `functionCall` part with a signature: emit the `ToolCallDelta`, then
  `ProviderData { provider: "gemini", call_id: Some(<the same call_id>), data: {"thoughtSignature": s} }`.
- For a part with a signature and no `functionCall` (a text part, or an empty text part at the end
  of the stream): emit `ProviderData { call_id: None, data: {"thoughtSignature": s} }` after the
  part's `TokenDelta`.
- A part that holds only a signature and an empty text emits no empty `TokenDelta`. (The builder
  checks the existing behavior for `text: ""` and keeps it if a test depends on it.)

### Gemini request translator (`translate/request.rs`)

- While it walks the items, the translator keeps the Gemini `ProviderData` parts of the last
  `AssistantMessage` as pending signatures: a list of `(call_id, signature)` and at most one
  message-level signature. Parts of another provider are ignored without a warning. The
  `ProviderData` part itself never becomes a wire part.
- A `functionCall` (from `Item::ToolCall` or `ContentPart::ToolUse`) takes the first pending
  signature with the same `call_id` and removes it. The signature goes on the same part:
  `{"functionCall": {...}, "thoughtSignature": "..."}`.
- The message-level signature goes on the last `text` part of that `AssistantMessage`. If the
  message has no text part, it is dropped. (Gemini documents a text signature as optional.)
- The pending list is cleared at the next `UserMessage` or `ToolResult` after the calls, so a
  signature never moves into a later turn.
- **Order:** Gemini puts the signature of a parallel call on the first `functionCall` part. Core
  sorts tool calls by `call_id`, so with native ids the signed call can come later. In each merged
  `model` content, the translator moves the signed `functionCall` parts before the unsigned ones and
  keeps the order otherwise. The probe showed that the order of `functionResponse` parts does not
  matter (SMA-820 shape 11). The live check below confirms whether the call order matters; if it
  does not, the move is still harmless.
- **History with no signatures:** a `model` content whose `functionCall` parts have no real
  signature gets the documented dummy `skip_thought_signature_validator` on each `functionCall`
  part. This is the shape that the SMA-820 probe proved (HTTP 200 on `gemini-3.8-flash`). A content
  that has a real signature on any of its calls is sent as received: the other calls stay unsigned,
  as Gemini returned them. Google says the dummy can make the answer worse, so it is only the
  fallback. The dummy goes into one `const` with a doc comment and the source.
- The SMA-820 tool-result boundary in `merge_same_role` stays as it is. Its doc comment changes:
  the reason is no longer "the SDK sends no signatures". See "Left for Sven".

### Live check (acceptance criterion, before code)

The Google pages that the builder can reach show no `generateContent` JSON for signatures, so the
wire format comes from a live capture. A probe script (bash, `curl`, `jq`) runs against the
Developer API on `gemini-3.8-flash` before any production code. It reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` from the
environment and never prints a header or the key. Sven runs it (the agent shell has no key), for
example with `! bash <scratchpad>/probe.sh`. Captures:

1. A streamed (`streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`) first turn that asks for two parallel calls. Record:
   where `thoughtSignature` sits, which parts carry it, whether `functionCall.id` is present, and
   whether the signature arrives in the same chunk as its call.
2. A streamed turn with a text answer: does a text part or an empty last part carry a signature?
3. Second turn with the real signature on the call, as received: expect HTTP 200.
4. Second turn, parallel calls, real signature on a call that is **not** first: record the result.
5. Second turn with the dummy on each call: expect HTTP 200.
6. SMA-820 shape 3 (`user[functionResponse, text]` merged) with the real signature: record the
   result, for the boundary decision.

If capture 1 shows a different wire shape than this design expects, stop and bring it to Sven
before the code. The probe source and its results go into the PR body.

## Tests

- Core: accumulator unit tests: a tool-only turn with provider data gives
  `[AssistantMessage[ProviderData], ToolCall]`; text plus provider data keeps the order
  `Reasoning, Text, ProviderData`; no provider data gives the same items as today.
- Core: `tests/serde_roundtrip.rs` gets `content_part_provider_data_roundtrip` (with and without
  `call_id`) and a new snapshot. Existing snapshots do not change.
- Core: runner final output is not erased by a ProviderData-only message (a run that ends after a
  tool-only turn keeps the earlier text). Workflow `assistant_text` returns `None` for it.
- Gemini stream: a signed `functionCall` gives a `ToolCallDelta` and then `ProviderData` with the
  same `call_id`; a signed text part gives `ProviderData` with `call_id: None`; a part with no
  signature gives no `ProviderData`. Use fixtures copied from the live capture.
- Gemini request (unit tests and insta snapshots): the signature round trip from stream events to
  `ModelTurn` to request JSON; repeated `fc_0` across two turns keeps each signature in its own
  turn; parallel calls where the signed id sorts after an unsigned id (`fc_10` vs `fc_2`, and two
  native ids) put the signed call first; a history with no signatures gets the dummy on each call;
  a foreign `ProviderData` part is ignored; a ProviderData-only message emits no `model` content.
- OpenAI Chat and LiteLLM: the two empty-message cases above.
- Live (`tests/live.rs`, `#[ignore]`): a two-turn tool loop through `GeminiModel::invoke` on
  `gemini-3.8-flash`, where the history after the tool result has **no** trailing user text, so the
  call is in the current turn. It must end with `Finish` and no error. A second live test runs the
  same loop through `LlmAgent` with a real tool, so the accumulator path is covered.

## Docs and release

- The core rustdoc on both variants states the contract above.
- The mdBook: update the page that lists `ContentPart` / `ModelEvent` variants, if one exists, and
  the Gemini provider page (tool loops on Gemini 3 now work).
- `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/README.md`: note the signature support only if it lists
  limits today.
- Release: release-plz bumps the touched crates (additive, patch on 0.x) and cascades the facade. No
  hand bump. cargo-semver-checks must stay green: new variants on `#[non_exhaustive]` enums are not
  breaking.

## Left to the builder

- The exact names of private helpers and the pending-signature struct.
- Whether the probe uses `jq` or a short Rust example. Bash plus `jq` is the default.
- How to keep the dummy-signature tests readable (a helper that builds a signed history).

## Left for Sven

- **The SMA-820 tool-result boundary.** With real signatures (and the dummy as fallback), every
  call is signed, so the merged shape `user[functionResponse, text]` probably gets HTTP 200, and
  the boundary may not be necessary. Capture 6 gives the evidence. My proposal: keep the boundary
  in this PR, because it changes nothing that works today, and decide on its removal with the
  capture result.
- **The Anthropic follow-up ticket.** I file it in Linear after the spec is approved.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SMA-827 live probe: Gemini 3 thoughtSignature wire format and round trip.
# Reads GEMINI_API_KEY from the environment. Never prints headers or the key.
# Usage: GEMINI_MODEL_ID=gemini-3.8-flash bash probe.sh
set -euo pipefail

: "${GEMINI_API_KEY:?set GEMINI_API_KEY}"
MODEL="${GEMINI_MODEL_ID:-gemini-3.8-flash}"
BASE="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/${MODEL}"
OUT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)/probe-out"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
DUMMY="skip_thought_signature_validator"

TOOLS='[{"functionDeclarations":[
  {"name":"search","description":"Search the web","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string"}},"required":["q"]}},
  {"name":"weather","description":"Get the weather for a city","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"city":{"type":"string"}},"required":["city"]}}
]}]'

post() { # $1=method suffix, $2=body file, $3=out file -> prints HTTP code
  curl -s -o "$3" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "${BASE}:$1" \
    -H "x-goog-api-key: ${GEMINI_API_KEY}" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data-binary @"$2"
}

summarize_sse() { # one line per part: chunk index, keys, id, signature length
  grep '^data: ' "$1" | sed 's/^data: //' | jq -c --slurp '
    to_entries[] | .key as $c | (.value.candidates[0].content.parts // [])[] |
    {chunk:$c, keys:(keys), fc_id:(.functionCall.id // null), fc_name:(.functionCall.name // null),
     text_len:((.text // null) | if .==null then null else length end),
     sig_len:((.thoughtSignature // null) | if .==null then null else length end)}'
  echo "finishReasons:"; grep '^data: ' "$1" | sed 's/^data: //' | jq -r '.candidates[0].finishReason // empty'
}

model_parts() { # all parts of the streamed model turn, in order
  grep '^data: ' "$1" | sed 's/^data: //' | jq -c --slurp '[.[].candidates[0].content.parts // [] | .[]]'
}

second_turn() { # $1=name, $2=jq filter applied to the model parts array, $3=extra user parts (json array)
  local parts responses body
  parts="$(model_parts "$OUT/1-parallel.sse" | jq -c "$2")"
  responses="$(echo "$parts" | jq -c '[.[] | select(.functionCall) |
    {functionResponse:{id:.functionCall.id, name:.functionCall.name,
      response:(if .functionCall.name=="search" then {hits:3} else {temp_c:18} end)}}]')"
  body="$OUT/$1.req.json"
  jq -n --argjson tools "$TOOLS" --argjson mp "$parts" --argjson fr "$responses" --argjson extra "$3" '
    {tools:$tools, contents:[
      {role:"user", parts:[{text:"Search for cats and get the weather in Paris. Call both tools now, in parallel."}]},
      {role:"model", parts:$mp},
      {role:"user", parts:($fr + $extra)}]}' > "$body"
  local code; code="$(post generateContent "$body" "$OUT/$1.resp.json")"
  printf '%-28s HTTP %s  finish=%s  %s\n' "$1" "$code" \
    "$(jq -r '.candidates[0].finishReason // "-"' "$OUT/$1.resp.json")" \
    "$(jq -r '.error.message // (.candidates[0].content.parts | map(.text // (.functionCall.name|tostring)) | join(" ") | .[0:80]) // ""' "$OUT/$1.resp.json")"
}

echo "== model: $MODEL"
echo "== 1. streamed parallel tool call"
jq -n --argjson tools "$TOOLS" '{tools:$tools, contents:[{role:"user", parts:[{text:"Search for cats and get the weather in Paris. Call both tools now, in parallel."}]}]}' > "$OUT/1.req.json"
echo "HTTP $(post 'streamGenerateContent?alt=sse' "$OUT/1.req.json" "$OUT/1-parallel.sse")"
summarize_sse "$OUT/1-parallel.sse"

echo "== 2. streamed text answer"
jq -n '{contents:[{role:"user", parts:[{text:"Explain in two sentences why the sky is blue."}]}]}' > "$OUT/2.req.json"
echo "HTTP $(post 'streamGenerateContent?alt=sse' "$OUT/2.req.json" "$OUT/2-text.sse")"
summarize_sse "$OUT/2-text.sse"

echo "== second turns (generateContent)"
second_turn 3-real-as-received '.' '[]'
second_turn 4-real-signed-last '([.[] | select(.thoughtSignature|not)] + [.[] | select(.thoughtSignature)])' '[]'
second_turn 5-dummy-each-call "[.[] | del(.thoughtSignature) | if .functionCall then . + {thoughtSignature:\"$DUMMY\"} else . end]" '[]'
second_turn 6-merged-text-real '.' '[{"text":"Now answer in one sentence."}]'
second_turn 7-no-signature '[.[] | del(.thoughtSignature)]' '[]'
echo "== raw files in $OUT"

---
name: project_release_ascend_needs_core_bump
description: "When a 0.0.0 stub crate ascends and uses paigasus-helikon-core API added in the same PR, you must also bump core's version or release-plz's publish fails."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6a9723cd-b6b1-44aa-a8bf-8c53c21a6501
---

The CLAUDE.md "4-step ascend recipe" (bump stub `0.0.0`→`0.1.0`, drop `publish = false`, remove the `release = false` block in `release-plz.toml`, bump the `[workspace.dependencies]` pin) is INSUFFICIENT when the ascending crate depends on `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR. `cargo publish --verify` builds the ascending crate's tarball against the **registry** core (the `path` is stripped at publish), so if the published core version lacks the new API the publish fails with compile errors (E0599/E0609 "no field/method/variant") → "failed to verify package tarball", and release-plz's combined job (SMA-351) aborts before its release-PR step → deadlock (core never gets an auto bump).

**Why:** release-plz publishes per Cargo.toml-version-vs-crates.io diff and ignores source changes that don't bump the version; a squashed PR commit scoped `feat(<ascending-crate>)` attributes nothing to core, so crates.io core stays at its old version without the new API.

**How to apply:** In the ascend PR, ALSO bump `paigasus-helikon-core` (patch for additive/non-breaking-behind-`#[non_exhaustive]`, e.g. `0.2.0`→`0.2.1`, matching release-plz's 0.x convention) plus its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin + CHANGELOG. release-plz then publishes core first, then the ascending crate (dependency-ordered) verifies against the fresh core. Diagnosed in SMA-321: PR #45 failed the release; PR #46 (`chore(release)` bumping core to 0.2.1) fixed it. Related: [[reference_crates_io_api_user_agent]] (preflight version checks need a custom UA).

**Complement — the manual bump is ONLY for the deadlock above; do NOT over-apply it to an already-released consumer.** The deadlock requires a crate whose Cargo.toml version is bumped *by hand* in the PR (the ascend `0.0.0`→`0.1.0`, or any manual bump), forcing release-plz's `release` step to publish it immediately — before release-plz has bumped core. If the consuming crate is **already released** (a real version, not a stub) and you do NOT hand-bump it, NOTHING publishes prematurely: release-plz bundles core + consumer + facade into one release PR and publishes them in dependency order (core lands on the registry before the consumer's `cargo publish --verify`), with the `dependencies_update` cascade to the facade intact. So for an already-released consumer adding+using same-PR core API, the correct play is **pure-auto** (no manual version/CHANGELOG edits at all) — and a manual same-PR core bump would actually *defeat* the cascade (the documented facade-drift second-order caveat). Reactive fallback if a publish ever deadlocks: a follow-up `chore(release):` PR (the SMA-321/SMA-346 pattern). Decided AND confirmed in SMA-418 (PR #80, `paigasus-helikon-tools` already at `0.1.2`): the ticket initially pattern-matched the ascend ritual; we shipped pure-auto instead. On merge, release-plz opened one `chore: release` PR (#81) bumping core `0.5.1→0.5.2`, tools `0.1.2→0.1.3`, AND every other core-dependent via the cascade (facade `0.3.8→0.3.9`, providers-openai/anthropic, sessions-sqlite, runtime-tokio, mcp — each a patch bump to refresh its core req); merging #81 published all of them to crates.io cleanly in dependency order (core first), no deadlock, no manual bump. So for an already-released consumer, pure-auto is the proven path — and note the cascade touches the WHOLE workspace (everything depends on core), which a by-hand bump can't replicate consistently.

35-
36:**Caveat — when the ascending crate uses `paigasus-helikon-core` API added in the *same* PR, bump `core` too** (a 5th step). `cargo publish --verify` builds the ascending crate's tarball against the **registry** core (the `path` is stripped at publish), so if crates.io `core` lacks the new API the publish fails with `failed to verify package tarball`, and release-plz's combined job (SMA-351) aborts before its release-PR step — a deadlock, since `core` never gets its auto bump (a squashed `feat(<ascending-crate>)` commit attributes nothing to `core`). Fix: in the same PR, also bump `paigasus-helikon-core` (patch for additive/non-breaking-behind-`#[non_exhaustive]`, e.g. `0.2.0` → `0.2.1`) and its `[workspace.dependencies]` pin + CHANGELOG. release-plz then publishes `core` first, then the ascending crate verifies against the fresh `core` (dependency-ordered publish). Diagnosed in SMA-321: PR #45's release failed against the stale `core` `0.2.0`; PR #46 (`chore(release)` bumping `core` to `0.2.1`) cleared it.
37-
38-## Caveat 2 — the manual core bump defeats the facade cascade (SMA-346)
39-
40:**Second-order caveat — the manual core bump silently defeats `dependencies_update`, so the facade drifts.** `release-plz.toml` sets `dependencies_update = true`, which is *supposed* to cascade: when a sibling's version changes, release-plz bumps the facade's `[workspace.dependencies]` pin and gives the facade a patch bump. But that cascade only runs when **release-plz itself performs the sibling bump**. The same-PR manual bump above means the sibling version is already at target when the PR merges, so release-plz just publishes it and never runs the dependent-bump step — the facade (`paigasus-helikon`) is left untouched and stops tracking. Consequence: the facade stays at its old version with stale published dep reqs (e.g. after SMA-346, facade `0.2.0` still requested `paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio = ^0.0.0`, so the new runner-boundary surface was unreachable through the facade's `runtime-tokio` feature). **Fix: in any PR that uses the same-PR manual bump, ALSO bump the facade** (patch: `version` in `crates/paigasus-helikon/Cargo.toml` + its `[workspace.dependencies]` self-pin + CHANGELOG) so it republishes with current sibling reqs. Diagnosed after SMA-346: PRs #48/#49 shipped `core 0.2.3` + `runtime-tokio 0.1.1` but left facade `0.2.0`; PR #50 (`chore(release)` bumping facade to `0.2.1`) cleared it. NB: feature branches must match the `branch-names` ruleset (`feature/**` or `hotfix/**`); a `chore/**` branch is rejected at push with `GH013 … creations being restricted`.
41-
42-## A red release-plz run with 403 on `git/refs` (SMA-745)
43-
44-**Symptom.** A `release-plz.yml` run fails with `403 Forbidden` and an empty body on `POST /repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/refs`. The failed call can create a release branch or a tag. On 2026-10-30, two runs failed this way. One run published `paigasus-helikon-evals` 0.1.17 to crates.io and then failed to create the tag. The crate had no tag and no GitHub release.
45-
46-**Cause.** GitHub refuses to create a ref at a commit that is behind workflow-file changes on `main`. The token needs the `workflow` permission for this. In both runs, a PR that changes `.github/workflows/*` merged while the run was in progress. We measured this on 2026-10-31 with an OAuth token that had no `workflow` scope. We did not use the App token. The same call, ref name and token gave different results:
47-
48-| Target commit | Position | Result |
49-| -- | -- | -- |
50-| A commit behind a workflow change on `main` | behind `main` | `404 Not Found`, no ref |
51-| The tip of `main` | tip of `main` | ref created |

One response can hold several thinking blocks, with `redacted_thinking` blocks between them. The API needs each block's text byte-exact with its signature, and it needs the block sequence unchanged. After the join, the follow-up cannot split the text again. When the turn has text, the signature is never directly after its Reasoning part. OpenAI Responses has the same problem: a `reasoning` item must come before the item that it produced, but the fixed order puts provider data after `Text`.
    - Why it matters: The contract is public rustdoc on a core type. Sven's requirement (carrier must later hold Anthropic thinking signatures and `redacted_thinking`) is not met by the stated mechanism.
    - Suggested fix: Choose one option now.
      - Option (a): Say that the position of the part has no meaning. Provider-data parts keep arrival order among themselves. A provider that needs block structure stores the whole block in `data`. For Anthropic that is `{"type":"thinking","thinking":…,"signature":…}` or `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":…}`. Its translator puts the blocks where its wire format needs them. The cost is that the thinking text is stored two times.
      - Option (b): The accumulator keeps the interleave. A `call_id: None` provider-data event closes the current Reasoning or Text run, so the content becomes `[Reasoning A, PD sigA, Reasoning B, PD sigB, Text]`. The shape changes only when provider data is present.
      - Remove the "immediately after its Reasoning part" sentence in either case.

    - What is wrong: OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Bedrock and LiteLLM already produce `AssistantMessage[Reasoning]` with no `Text` part (a reasoning plus tool-call turn). With the spec's guard, these effects change:

# SMA-827: Gemini thought signatures round trip through a provider-data part in core

Linear: [SMA-827](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-827). Related: SMA-820 (merge of same-role
contents, tool-result boundary), SMA-565 (stale `gemini-2.5-flash` ids).

## Intent

Gemini 3 models put a `thoughtSignature` on the `functionCall` parts of a response. The next
request must send each signature back on the same part. If a call in the current turn has no
signature, the API returns HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall
parts". The SDK reads no signature and sends none. So every tool loop on Gemini 3 fails at the
second model call. For a new user, every available Gemini model is a Gemini 3 model (the 2.x ids
return HTTP 404), so the Gemini provider cannot run a tool loop at all.

Core has no place for provider data. Anthropic has the same gap: its stream drops
`signature_delta` (`providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:122`) and its request translator drops
`ContentPart::Reasoning` ("signature round-trip not yet supported"). Sven decided on 2026-11-20
that the new core shape must also hold Anthropic thinking signatures. This PR fixes Gemini only.

## Goals

1. Core gets one general carrier for opaque provider data, in the stream and in the history. The
   carrier can hold a Gemini signature for a tool call now, and an Anthropic `thinking` or
   `redacted_thinking` block later.
2. The Gemini stream translator keeps the `thoughtSignature` and the stream position of each
   `functionCall` part.
3. The Gemini request translator sends each signature back on the same part, with the calls in the
   order that Gemini sent them.
4. A history with no valid signatures (a stored session from before this change, a history from
   another provider or another Gemini model, a hand-built history) still works on Gemini 3.
5. The signature survives the session store and the durable runners, because it lives in the item
   history. (A handoff drops all tool calls from the transcript, see `thread_handoff_transcript`,
   so a signature has no call to attach to after a handoff. That is correct, not a loss.)

## Non-goals

- The Anthropic round trip. A follow-up Linear ticket does it with the same carrier.
- OpenAI Responses `encrypted_content` reasoning items. The carrier can hold them later.
- **Text-level signatures.** Gemini can also put a signature on a text part. Google documents it as
  optional to return. Core joins all `TokenDelta`s into one `Text` part, so the SDK cannot send it
  back on the part where it came. This PR ignores it. So only tool turns, which fail today, get the
  new part, and a text-only turn keeps today's stored format.
- Gemini thought summaries (`includeThoughts`, `thought: true` parts, translator item D3).
- Gemini 3 through other paths: the OpenAI provider on Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and
  LiteLLM in front of Gemini 3. See "Left for Sven".
- Scripted evals (`evals/src/script.rs` `ScriptEvent`) cannot express the new event. No change.
- A new `AgentEvent` variant. Provider data stays inside `MessageOutput` items.
- An opt-out builder flag. Only tool turns change format, and those fail today without this change.
- SMA-565 (the stale model ids in the crate docs).

## Anti-goals

- A breaking change in core. Sven chose the additive approach (approach A).
- Provider data that reaches a translator it does not belong to, or that makes another provider's
  request invalid.
- A change to any behavior that users can see for a turn **without** provider data. This includes
  turns of other providers that today give `AssistantMessage[Reasoning]` with no `Text`.
- A change to the text output (final output, CLI, HTTP DTO `output`, workflow state, AG-UI frames)
  because a tool-only turn now has an `AssistantMessage`.

## Approaches

- **A. New additive variants (chosen by Sven on 2026-11-20).** Add `ModelEvent::ProviderData` and
  `ContentPart::ProviderData`. Both enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is not a breaking change,
  and core gets a patch bump. The data sits next to the call in the same `AssistantMessage`, not on
  the call. A tool-only turn now has an `AssistantMessage`, so the text consumers need a guard.
- **B. A new field on existing variants.** `provider_data` on `Item::ToolCall`,
  `ContentPart::ToolUse`, `ContentPart::Reasoning` and `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`. The data model
  is cleaner, but the variant fields are not `#[non_exhaustive]`: about 300 edits (130
  `Item::ToolCall` sites, 162 `ToolCallDelta` sites), broken user code, and a minor bump for core
  and every dependent. Rejected.
- **C. A signature cache in `GeminiModel` plus the dummy signature.** No core change, but the
  signatures do not survive a restart, a session store or a durable runner, and it does nothing
  for Anthropic. Rejected.

## Design

### Core types

```rust
// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs
ModelEvent::ProviderData {
    /// Wire-format key of the translator that owns `data`, for example "gemini".
    provider: String,
    /// The tool call that `data` belongs to, when it belongs to one.
    call_id: Option<String>,
    /// Opaque payload. Only the owning translator reads it.
    data: serde_json::Value,
}

// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/item.rs
ContentPart::ProviderData {
    provider: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    call_id: Option<String>,
    data: serde_json::Value,
}
```

Serde form: `{"type":"provider_data","provider":"gemini","call_id":"call_1","data":{...}}`.

The rustdoc of both variants states this contract:

- `provider` is a **wire-format key** that one translator owns. It is not `Model::provider()`.
  (OpenAI Chat and OpenAI Responses both report `"openai"`, but they will need different keys.)
  Each provider crate that writes provider data exports its key as a `pub const`, so that a host can
  filter or remove the data.
- A translator reads only the parts with its own key. It ignores every other part **without a
  warning**, and never fails because of one.
- The part is valid only inside an `Item::AssistantMessage`. Every translator ignores it in any
  other item.
- `call_id: Some(id)` means: the data belongs to the tool call with that id in the same model
  response (the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow the message, or a `ContentPart::ToolUse` in the
  same message). Call ids can repeat across responses.
- The position of a `ProviderData` part in `content` has **no meaning**. `ProviderData` parts keep
  their arrival order among themselves. A provider that needs block structure stores the whole
  block in `data`. (For the Anthropic follow-up: `{"type":"thinking","thinking":…,"signature":…}` or
  `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":…}`, and its translator puts the blocks where its wire format
  needs them. The cost is that the thinking text is stored two times.)
- **Rollback note:** a reader on an earlier core version fails on `provider_data` with "unknown
  variant". After the first Gemini 3 tool turn, a session store or a Temporal history holds this
  variant. Deploy readers and Temporal workflow workers before writers, and do not roll back core
  below this version on a deployment that has stored such a turn. (The same hazard is documented for
  `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred`, `session.rs:152-154`.)

### Core helper and the text guard

A new public helper on `Item`:

```rust
/// True for an `AssistantMessage` whose content is not empty and holds only
/// `ContentPart::ProviderData` parts.
pub fn is_provider_data_only(&self) -> bool
```

Such a message did not exist before this change. So every text consumer that skips it keeps
today's behavior exactly, for every provider. The guard uses this predicate, and **not** "has no
`Text` part" (that predicate would change the behavior of `AssistantMessage[Reasoning]` turns from
OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Bedrock and LiteLLM).

The session recorder needs the `MessageOutput` event (`session.rs:894`), so the event stays. These
consumers skip a provider-data-only message, so that they act as if the event did not exist:

- `runner.rs` `collect` and `collect_typed` (around lines 434 and 513).
- `workflow.rs` `assistant_text` and its callers in `workflow.rs` and `graph.rs`.
- `cli/src/repl.rs` (around line 221).
- `runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs` (around lines 366-392).
- `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` `RunResponse::from_events` (they already skip an empty text;
  the guard makes the rule explicit).

The builder searches the workspace for every other consumer of `MessageOutput` or of an
`AssistantMessage` in the item history that takes text, and applies the same guard. The
structured-output path (`loop_state.rs` `last_assistant_content`) runs only on a turn with no tool
calls, so a provider-data-only message cannot reach it. The builder confirms that with a test.

### Core accumulator (`ModelTurnAccumulator`, `build_items`)

- `observe` keeps each `ModelEvent::ProviderData` in arrival order, in a new field.
- `build_items` makes the `AssistantMessage` when text, reasoning **or** provider data is not empty.
  Content order: `Reasoning`, `Text`, then the `ProviderData` parts in arrival order.
- Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items after the message, in the existing `call_id`-sorted order.
- The rustdoc of `ModelTurn::items` changes to say the message can hold provider data only.

### Core: the other places that match on the new variants

- `token_counter.rs` `part_chars`: `ProviderData` counts as 0 characters, because it is not
  model-visible text and only the owning provider sends it. The probe records whether
  `promptTokenCount` changes with the real signature against the dummy. If it changes a lot, the
  builder brings it back before the plan is final.
- `agent.rs` event forwarding (around line 1475): `ModelEvent::ProviderData` is not forwarded as an
  `AgentEvent`. The accumulator still observes it.
- `agent.rs` injection allow-list (around line 1298) already rejects an unknown part. No change.
- The provider-stream conformance suite (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/check.rs`) gets a
  rule: a `ProviderData` with `call_id: Some(id)` names an id of a `ToolCallDelta` in the same
  stream.

### Other provider translators

Each translator already drops an unknown part with a wildcard arm. The changes:

- **OpenAI Chat and LiteLLM.** Today they emit `{"role":"assistant","content":""}` for an
  `AssistantMessage` with only unknown parts. When `Item::ToolCall` items follow, they merge into
  that message, and the result is valid. Alone, it is an empty assistant message. Change: an
  assistant message with no text and no tool calls is not emitted, and the following tool calls
  still form one assistant message. A `UserMessage` with only provider data must not emit
  `{"role":"user","content":[]}`.
- **Bedrock.** Add an explicit silent arm for `ProviderData`, so it does not warn on each request.
- **Anthropic, OpenAI Responses.** They already send nothing for an empty message. Add an explicit
  silent arm where a wildcard would warn.
- **Gemini `user_parts`.** Add an explicit silent arm.

### Gemini stream translator (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)

A capture in the repo (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs:2225-2274`,
`gemini-3.6-flash`, 2026-08-20) shows: `functionCall.id` is present (`"call_1285087"`),
`thoughtSignature` is a sibling of `functionCall` in the same part (about 700 characters), and the
`STOP` chunk carries `{"text":""}` with no signature. The probe checks this again on 3.8.

- `sse.rs` `Part` gets `thought_signature: Option<String>` (`thoughtSignature` on the wire).
- For each `functionCall` part, the translator emits the `ToolCallDelta`, then
  `ProviderData { provider: "gemini", call_id: Some(<the same call_id>), data }`, where `data` is:

  ```json
  { "index": 0, "thoughtSignature": "<opaque>", "model": "gemini-3.8-flash", "api": "developer" }
  ```

  - `index` is the position of the call among the `functionCall` parts of this response (0, 1, 2,
    …), counted across chunks. It is present on **every** call, signed or not.
  - `thoughtSignature` is present only when the part has one.
  - `model` is the configured model id. `api` is `"developer"` or `"vertex"`. Both are present only
    with a signature.
- The `call_id` is the native id when present. Otherwise it is the existing synthesized
  `fc_<n>`. The request translator sends the same `call_id` as `functionCall.id`, so the pair matches
  in both directions.
- A signature on a part with no `functionCall` is ignored (see the text-level non-goal).
- The key `"gemini"` is exported as a `pub const` of the Gemini crate. The Developer API and Vertex
  share the translator, so they share the key, and `api` tells them apart.

### Gemini request translator (`translate/request.rs`)

**Pairing.** For each `AssistantMessage`, the translator first reads all its Gemini `ProviderData`
parts into a pending list of `(call_id, data)`. Then each `functionCall` (from a `ToolUse` part in
the same message, or from the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow) takes the first pending entry with
the same `call_id` and removes it. The pending list is cleared at the next `AssistantMessage` and at
the next `UserMessage` that is not only tool results. A `ToolResult` does not clear it, because
`close_open_transfers` can put a result between two calls of one response
(`resume_exec.rs:185,194`). The `ProviderData` part itself never becomes a wire part.

Trade-off for damaged histories: if items of two responses with the same call ids interleave with
no `AssistantMessage` between them, a signature can attach to the wrong call. Core never writes that
shape. The result is at worst an HTTP 400 for a history that is already damaged.

**Valid signature.** A signature is valid for this request when `data.model` equals the configured
model id and `data.api` equals the configured transport. A signature that is missing, malformed (not
a string) or not valid is treated as absent. A malformed part never causes an error.

**Order.** In each merged `model` content, when every `functionCall` part has an `index`, the
translator sorts the `functionCall` parts by `index` and keeps the other parts where they are. This
restores the order that Gemini sent. Otherwise the order stays as in the history.

**Signature on the part.** A valid signature goes on the same part:
`{"functionCall": {...}, "thoughtSignature": "..."}`.

**Fallback (dummy signature).** The current turn is every content after the last `user` content
that holds no `functionResponse` part. (SMA-820 shapes 2 and 4: Gemini checks signatures only in that
turn. The tool-result boundary keeps a text in its own content, so a mixed content is not built.) In
the current turn, a `model` content whose `functionCall` parts have no valid signature gets the
documented dummy `skip_thought_signature_validator` on each `functionCall` part. The SMA-820 probe
proved this shape (HTTP 200 on `gemini-3.8-flash`). Outside the current turn, no dummy is added.
This is a hard rule: a content with at least one valid signature is sent as received, and the
other calls stay unsigned, as Gemini returned them. Google says the dummy can make the answer worse,
so it is only the fallback. The dummy goes into one `const` with a doc comment and its source.

**SMA-820 boundary.** The tool-result boundary in `merge_same_role` stays. Its doc comment changes:
the reason is no longer "the SDK sends no signatures". See "Left for Sven".

### Live check (before the Gemini code)

The Google pages that can be reached show no `generateContent` JSON for signatures, so the wire
format comes from live captures. The probe (bash, `curl`, `jq`) runs against the Developer API on
`gemini-3.8-flash`. It reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` from the environment and never prints a header or the
key. Sven runs it, because the agent shell has no key. Captures:

1. A streamed first turn that asks for three parallel calls. Record: where `thoughtSignature` sits,
   which parts carry it, whether `functionCall.id` is present, and whether the signature arrives in
   the same chunk as its call.
2. A streamed text answer: record whether a part carries a signature (information only).
3. Second turn, real signatures as received: expect HTTP 200.
4. Second turn, the signed call moved to the last position: record the result.
5. Second turn, the signed call first and the two unsigned calls swapped: record the result.
6. Second turn, the dummy on each call: expect HTTP 200. Compare `promptTokenCount` with capture 3.
7. Second turn, no signature: expect HTTP 400 (control).
8. SMA-820 shape 3 (`user[functionResponse…, text]` merged) with the real signature: record the
   result, for the boundary decision.
9. When `GEMINI_MODEL_ID_2` is set: capture 3 sent to the second model. Record whether Gemini
   accepts a signature from another model.

The core work and the work in other crates do not depend on the wire shape, so they can start
before the probe results. The Gemini stream and request work waits for the results. If capture 1
shows a different wire shape than this design expects, stop and bring it to Sven. Fixtures are
transcribed from the captures, with each real signature replaced by a placeholder. No real
signature goes into the repo or the PR body. Vertex is not probed; the spec states this limit in the
Gemini README.

## Tests

- **Core accumulator:** a tool-only turn with provider data gives
  `[AssistantMessage[ProviderData…], ToolCall…]`; text plus provider data gives the order
  `Reasoning, Text, ProviderData`; no provider data gives the same items as today.

# SMA-827: Gemini thought signatures round trip through a provider-data part in core

Linear: [SMA-827](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-827). Related: SMA-820 (merge of same-role
contents, tool-result boundary), SMA-565 (stale `gemini-2.5-flash` ids).

## Intent

Gemini 3 models put a `thoughtSignature` on the `functionCall` parts of a response. The next
request must send each signature back on the same part. If a call in the current turn has no
signature, the API returns HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall
parts". The SDK reads no signature and sends none. So every tool loop on Gemini 3 fails at the
second model call. For a new user, every available Gemini model is a Gemini 3 model (the 2.x ids
return HTTP 404), so the Gemini provider cannot run a tool loop at all.

Core has no place for provider data. Anthropic has the same gap: its stream drops
`signature_delta` (`providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:122`) and its request translator drops
`ContentPart::Reasoning` ("signature round-trip not yet supported"). Sven decided on 2026-11-20
that the new core shape must also hold Anthropic thinking signatures. This PR fixes Gemini only.

## Goals

1. Core gets one general carrier for opaque provider data, in the stream and in the history. The
   carrier can hold a Gemini signature for a tool call now, and an Anthropic `thinking` or
   `redacted_thinking` block later.
2. The Gemini stream translator keeps the `thoughtSignature` and the stream position of each
   `functionCall` part.
3. The Gemini request translator sends each signature back on the same part, with the calls in the
   order that Gemini sent them.
4. A history with no valid signatures (a stored session from before this change, a history from
   another provider or another Gemini model, a hand-built history) still works on Gemini 3.
5. The signature survives the session store and the durable runners, because it lives in the item
   history. (A handoff drops all tool calls from the transcript, see `thread_handoff_transcript`,
   so a signature has no call to attach to after a handoff. That is correct, not a loss.)

## Non-goals

- The Anthropic round trip. A follow-up Linear ticket does it with the same carrier.
- OpenAI Responses `encrypted_content` reasoning items. The carrier can hold them later.
- **Text-level signatures.** Gemini can also put a signature on a text part. Google documents it as
  optional to return. Core joins all `TokenDelta`s into one `Text` part, so the SDK cannot send it
  back on the part where it came. This PR ignores it. So only tool turns, which fail today, get the
  new part, and a text-only turn keeps today's stored format.
- Gemini thought summaries (`includeThoughts`, `thought: true` parts, translator item D3).
- Gemini 3 through other paths: the OpenAI provider on Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and
  LiteLLM in front of Gemini 3. See "Left for Sven".
- Scripted evals (`evals/src/script.rs` `ScriptEvent`) cannot express the new event. No change.
- A new `AgentEvent` variant. Provider data stays inside `MessageOutput` items.
- An opt-out builder flag. Only tool turns change format, and those fail today without this change.
- SMA-565 (the stale model ids in the crate docs).

## Anti-goals

- A breaking change in core. Sven chose the additive approach (approach A).
- Provider data that reaches a translator it does not belong to, or that makes another provider's
  request invalid.
- A change to any behavior that users can see for a turn **without** provider data. This includes
  turns of other providers that today give `AssistantMessage[Reasoning]` with no `Text`.
- A change to the text output (final output, CLI, HTTP DTO `output`, workflow state, AG-UI frames)
  because a tool-only turn now has an `AssistantMessage`.

## Approaches

- **A. New additive variants (chosen by Sven on 2026-11-20).** Add `ModelEvent::ProviderData` and
  `ContentPart::ProviderData`. Both enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is not a breaking change,
  and core gets a patch bump. The data sits next to the call in the same `AssistantMessage`, not on
  the call. A tool-only turn now has an `AssistantMessage`, so the text consumers need a guard.
- **B. A new field on existing variants.** `provider_data` on `Item::ToolCall`,
  `ContentPart::ToolUse`, `ContentPart::Reasoning` and `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`. The data model
  is cleaner, but the variant fields are not `#[non_exhaustive]`: about 300 edits (130
  `Item::ToolCall` sites, 162 `ToolCallDelta` sites), broken user code, and a minor bump for core
  and every dependent. Rejected.
- **C. A signature cache in `GeminiModel` plus the dummy signature.** No core change, but the
  signatures do not survive a restart, a session store or a durable runner, and it does nothing
  for Anthropic. Rejected.

## Design

### Core types

```rust
// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs
ModelEvent::ProviderData {
    /// Wire-format key of the translator that owns `data`, for example "gemini".
    provider: String,
    /// The tool call that `data` belongs to, when it belongs to one.
    call_id: Option<String>,
    /// Opaque payload. Only the owning translator reads it.
    data: serde_json::Value,
}

// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/item.rs
ContentPart::ProviderData {
    provider: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    call_id: Option<String>,
    data: serde_json::Value,
}
```

Serde form: `{"type":"provider_data","provider":"gemini","call_id":"call_1","data":{...}}`.

The rustdoc of both variants states this contract:

- `provider` is a **wire-format key** that one translator owns. It is not `Model::provider()`.
  (OpenAI Chat and OpenAI Responses both report `"openai"`, but they will need different keys.)
  Each provider crate that writes provider data exports its key as a `pub const`, so that a host can
  filter or remove the data.
- A translator reads only the parts with its own key. It ignores every other part **without a
  warning**, and never fails because of one.
- The part is valid only inside an `Item::AssistantMessage`. Every translator ignores it in any
  other item.
- `call_id: Some(id)` means: the data belongs to the tool call with that id in the same model
  response (the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow the message, or a `ContentPart::ToolUse` in the
  same message). Call ids can repeat across responses.
- The position of a `ProviderData` part in `content` has **no meaning**. `ProviderData` parts keep
  their arrival order among themselves. A provider that needs block structure stores the whole
  block in `data`. (For the Anthropic follow-up: `{"type":"thinking","thinking":…,"signature":…}` or
  `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":…}`, and its translator puts the blocks where its wire format
  needs them. The cost is that the thinking text is stored two times.)
- **Rollback note:** a reader on an earlier core version fails on `provider_data` with "unknown
  variant". After the first Gemini 3 tool turn, a session store or a Temporal history holds this
  variant. Deploy readers and Temporal workflow workers before writers, and do not roll back core
  below this version on a deployment that has stored such a turn. (The same hazard is documented for
  `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred`, `session.rs:152-154`.)

### Core helper and the text guard

A new public helper on `Item`:

```rust
/// True for an `AssistantMessage` whose content is not empty and holds only
/// `ContentPart::ProviderData` parts.
pub fn is_provider_data_only(&self) -> bool
```

Such a message did not exist before this change. So every text consumer that skips it keeps
today's behavior exactly, for every provider. The guard uses this predicate, and **not** "has no
`Text` part" (that predicate would change the behavior of `AssistantMessage[Reasoning]` turns from
OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Bedrock and LiteLLM).

The session recorder needs the `MessageOutput` event (`session.rs:894`), so the event stays. These
consumers skip a provider-data-only message, so that they act as if the event did not exist:

- `runner.rs` `collect` and `collect_typed` (around lines 434 and 513).
- `workflow.rs` `assistant_text` and its callers in `workflow.rs` and `graph.rs`.
- `cli/src/repl.rs` (around line 221).
- `runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs` (around lines 366-392).
- `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` `RunResponse::from_events` (they already skip an empty text;
  the guard makes the rule explicit).

The builder searches the workspace for every other consumer of `MessageOutput` or of an
`AssistantMessage` in the item history that takes text, and applies the same guard. The
structured-output path (`loop_state.rs` `last_assistant_content`) runs only on a turn with no tool
calls, so a provider-data-only message cannot reach it. The builder confirms that with a test.

### Core accumulator (`ModelTurnAccumulator`, `build_items`)

- `observe` keeps each `ModelEvent::ProviderData` in arrival order, in a new field.
- `build_items` makes the `AssistantMessage` when text, reasoning **or** provider data is not empty.
  Content order: `Reasoning`, `Text`, then the `ProviderData` parts in arrival order.
- Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items after the message, in the existing `call_id`-sorted order.
- The rustdoc of `ModelTurn::items` changes to say the message can hold provider data only.

### Core: the other places that match on the new variants

- `token_counter.rs` `part_chars`: `ProviderData` counts as 0 characters, because it is not
  model-visible text and only the owning provider sends it. The probe records whether
  `promptTokenCount` changes with the real signature against the dummy. If it changes a lot, the
  builder brings it back before the plan is final.
- `agent.rs` event forwarding (around line 1475): `ModelEvent::ProviderData` is not forwarded as an
  `AgentEvent`. The accumulator still observes it.
- `agent.rs` injection allow-list (around line 1298) already rejects an unknown part. No change.
- The provider-stream conformance suite (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/check.rs`) gets a
  rule: a `ProviderData` with `call_id: Some(id)` names an id of a `ToolCallDelta` in the same
  stream.

### Other provider translators

Each translator already drops an unknown part with a wildcard arm. The changes:

- **OpenAI Chat and LiteLLM.** Today they emit `{"role":"assistant","content":""}` for an
  `AssistantMessage` with only unknown parts. When `Item::ToolCall` items follow, they merge into
  that message, and the result is valid. Alone, it is an empty assistant message. Change: an
  assistant message with no text and no tool calls is not emitted, and the following tool calls
  still form one assistant message. A `UserMessage` with only provider data must not emit
  `{"role":"user","content":[]}`.
- **Bedrock.** Add an explicit silent arm for `ProviderData`, so it does not warn on each request.
- **Anthropic, OpenAI Responses.** They already send nothing for an empty message. Add an explicit
  silent arm where a wildcard would warn.
- **Gemini `user_parts`.** Add an explicit silent arm.

### Gemini stream translator (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)

A capture in the repo (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs:2225-2274`,
`gemini-3.6-flash`, 2026-08-20) shows: `functionCall.id` is present (`"call_1285087"`),
`thoughtSignature` is a sibling of `functionCall` in the same part (about 700 characters), and the
`STOP` chunk carries `{"text":""}` with no signature. The probe checks this again on 3.8.

- `sse.rs` `Part` gets `thought_signature: Option<String>` (`thoughtSignature` on the wire).
- For each `functionCall` part, the translator emits the `ToolCallDelta`, then
  `ProviderData { provider: "gemini", call_id: Some(<the same call_id>), data }`, where `data` is:

  ```json
  { "index": 0, "thoughtSignature": "<opaque>", "model": "gemini-3.8-flash", "api": "developer" }
  ```

  - `index` is the position of the call among the `functionCall` parts of this response (0, 1, 2,
    …), counted across chunks. It is present on **every** call, signed or not.
  - `thoughtSignature` is present only when the part has one.
  - `model` is the configured model id. `api` is `"developer"` or `"vertex"`. Both are present only
    with a signature.
- The `call_id` is the native id when present. Otherwise it is the existing synthesized
  `fc_<n>`. The request translator sends the same `call_id` as `functionCall.id`, so the pair matches
  in both directions.
- A signature on a part with no `functionCall` is ignored (see the text-level non-goal).
- The key `"gemini"` is exported as a `pub const` of the Gemini crate. The Developer API and Vertex
  share the translator, so they share the key, and `api` tells them apart.

### Gemini request translator (`translate/request.rs`)

**Pairing.** For each `AssistantMessage`, the translator first reads all its Gemini `ProviderData`
parts into a pending list of `(call_id, data)`. Then each `functionCall` (from a `ToolUse` part in
the same message, or from the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow) takes the first pending entry with
the same `call_id` and removes it. The pending list is cleared at the next `AssistantMessage` and at
the next `UserMessage` that is not only tool results. A `ToolResult` does not clear it, because
`close_open_transfers` can put a result between two calls of one response
(`resume_exec.rs:185,194`). The `ProviderData` part itself never becomes a wire part.

Trade-off for damaged histories: if items of two responses with the same call ids interleave with
no `AssistantMessage` between them, a signature can attach to the wrong call. Core never writes that
shape. The result is at worst an HTTP 400 for a history that is already damaged.

**Valid signature.** A signature is valid for this request when `data.model` equals the configured
model id and `data.api` equals the configured transport. A signature that is missing, malformed (not
a string) or not valid is treated as absent. A malformed part never causes an error.

**Order.** In each merged `model` content, when every `functionCall` part has an `index`, the
translator sorts the `functionCall` parts by `index` and keeps the other parts where they are. This
restores the order that Gemini sent. Otherwise the order stays as in the history.

**Signature on the part.** A valid signature goes on the same part:
`{"functionCall": {...}, "thoughtSignature": "..."}`.

**Fallback (dummy signature).** The current turn is every content after the last `user` content
that holds no `functionResponse` part. (SMA-820 shapes 2 and 4: Gemini checks signatures only in that
turn. The tool-result boundary keeps a text in its own content, so a mixed content is not built.) In
the current turn, a `model` content whose `functionCall` parts have no valid signature gets the
documented dummy `skip_thought_signature_validator` on each `functionCall` part. The SMA-820 probe
proved this shape (HTTP 200 on `gemini-3.8-flash`). Outside the current turn, no dummy is added.
This is a hard rule: a content with at least one valid signature is sent as received, and the
other calls stay unsigned, as Gemini returned them. Google says the dummy can make the answer worse,
so it is only the fallback. The dummy goes into one `const` with a doc comment and its source.

**SMA-820 boundary.** The tool-result boundary in `merge_same_role` stays. Its doc comment changes:
the reason is no longer "the SDK sends no signatures". See "Left for Sven".

### Live check (before the Gemini code)

The Google pages that can be reached show no `generateContent` JSON for signatures, so the wire
format comes from live captures. The probe (bash, `curl`, `jq`) runs against the Developer API on
`gemini-3.8-flash`. It reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` from the environment and never prints a header or the
key. Sven runs it, because the agent shell has no key. Captures:

1. A streamed first turn that asks for three parallel calls. Record: where `thoughtSignature` sits,
   which parts carry it, whether `functionCall.id` is present, and whether the signature arrives in
   the same chunk as its call.
2. A streamed text answer: record whether a part carries a signature (information only).
3. Second turn, real signatures as received: expect HTTP 200.
4. Second turn, the signed call moved to the last position: record the result.
5. Second turn, the signed call first and the two unsigned calls swapped: record the result.
6. Second turn, the dummy on each call: expect HTTP 200. Compare `promptTokenCount` with capture 3.
7. Second turn, no signature: expect HTTP 400 (control).
8. SMA-820 shape 3 (`user[functionResponse…, text]` merged) with the real signature: record the
   result, for the boundary decision.
9. When `GEMINI_MODEL_ID_2` is set: capture 3 sent to the second model. Record whether Gemini
   accepts a signature from another model.

The core work and the work in other crates do not depend on the wire shape, so they can start
before the probe results. The Gemini stream and request work waits for the results. If capture 1
shows a different wire shape than this design expects, stop and bring it to Sven. Fixtures are
transcribed from the captures, with each real signature replaced by a placeholder. No real
signature goes into the repo or the PR body. Vertex is not probed; the spec states this limit in the
Gemini README.

## Tests

  `[AssistantMessage[ProviderData…], ToolCall…]`; text plus provider data gives the order
  `Reasoning, Text, ProviderData`; no provider data gives the same items as today.
- **Core serde:** `tests/serde_roundtrip.rs` gets `content_part_provider_data_roundtrip` (with and
  without `call_id`) and a new snapshot. A `ModelTurn` with provider data survives a serde round
  trip (the Temporal `ModelTurnResult` path). Existing snapshots do not change.

  reasoning-only messages.

- Scripted evals (`evals/src/script.rs` `ScriptEvent`) cannot express the new event. No change.
- A new `AgentEvent` variant. Provider data stays inside `MessageOutput` items.
- An opt-out builder flag. Only tool turns change format, and those fail today without this change.
- SMA-565 (the stale model ids in the crate docs).

## Anti-goals

- A breaking change in core. Sven chose the additive approach (approach A).
- Provider data that reaches a translator it does not belong to, or that makes another provider's
  request invalid.
- A change to any behavior that users can see for a turn **without** provider data. This includes
  turns of other providers that today give `AssistantMessage[Reasoning]` with no `Text`.
- A change to the text output (final output, CLI, HTTP DTO `output`, workflow state, AG-UI frames)
  because a tool-only turn now has an `AssistantMessage`.

## Approaches

- **A. New additive variants (chosen by Sven on 2026-11-20).** Add `ModelEvent::ProviderData` and
  `ContentPart::ProviderData`. Both enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this is not a breaking change,
  and core gets a patch bump. The data sits next to the call in the same `AssistantMessage`, not on
  the call. A tool-only turn now has an `AssistantMessage`, so the text consumers need a guard.
- **B. A new field on existing variants.** `provider_data` on `Item::ToolCall`,
  `ContentPart::ToolUse`, `ContentPart::Reasoning` and `ModelEvent::ToolCallDelta`. The data model
  is cleaner, but the variant fields are not `#[non_exhaustive]`: about 300 edits (130
  `Item::ToolCall` sites, 162 `ToolCallDelta` sites), broken user code, and a minor bump for core
  and every dependent. Rejected.
- **C. A signature cache in `GeminiModel` plus the dummy signature.** No core change, but the
  signatures do not survive a restart, a session store or a durable runner, and it does nothing
  for Anthropic. Rejected.

## Design

### Core types

```rust
// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs
ModelEvent::ProviderData {
    /// Wire-format key of the translator that owns `data`, for example "gemini".
    provider: String,
    /// The tool call that `data` belongs to, when it belongs to one.
    call_id: Option<String>,
    /// Opaque payload. Only the owning translator reads it.
    data: serde_json::Value,
}

// crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/item.rs
ContentPart::ProviderData {
    provider: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    call_id: Option<String>,
    data: serde_json::Value,
}
```

Serde form: `{"type":"provider_data","provider":"gemini","call_id":"call_1","data":{...}}`.

The rustdoc of both variants states this contract:

- `provider` is a **wire-format key** that one translator owns. It is not `Model::provider()`.
  (OpenAI Chat and OpenAI Responses both report `"openai"`, but they will need different keys.)
  Each provider crate that writes provider data exports its key as a `pub const`, so that a host can
  filter or remove the data.
- A translator reads only the parts with its own key. It ignores every other part **without a
  warning**, and never fails because of one.
- The part is valid only inside an `Item::AssistantMessage`. Every translator ignores it in any
  other item.
- `call_id: Some(id)` means: the data belongs to the tool call with that id in the same model
  response (the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow the message, or a `ContentPart::ToolUse` in the
  same message). Call ids can repeat across responses.
- The position of a `ProviderData` part in `content` has **no meaning**. `ProviderData` parts keep
  their arrival order among themselves. A provider that needs block structure stores the whole
  block in `data`. (For the Anthropic follow-up: `{"type":"thinking","thinking":…,"signature":…}` or
  `{"type":"redacted_thinking","data":…}`, and its translator puts the blocks where its wire format
  needs them. The cost is that the thinking text is stored two times.)
- **Rollback note:** a reader on an earlier core version fails on `provider_data` with "unknown
  variant". After the first Gemini 3 tool turn, a session store or a Temporal history holds this
  variant. Deploy readers and Temporal workflow workers before writers, and do not roll back core
  below this version on a deployment that has stored such a turn. (The same hazard is documented for
  `SessionEvent::ToolDeferred`, `session.rs:152-154`.)

### Core helper and the text guard

A new public helper on `Item`:

```rust
/// True for an `AssistantMessage` whose content is not empty and holds only
/// `ContentPart::ProviderData` parts.
pub fn is_provider_data_only(&self) -> bool
```

Such a message did not exist before this change. So every text consumer that skips it keeps
today's behavior exactly, for every provider. The guard uses this predicate, and **not** "has no
`Text` part" (that predicate would change the behavior of `AssistantMessage[Reasoning]` turns from
OpenAI Responses, Anthropic, Bedrock and LiteLLM).

The session recorder needs the `MessageOutput` event (`session.rs:894`), so the event stays. These
consumers skip a provider-data-only message, so that they act as if the event did not exist:

- `runner.rs` `collect` and `collect_typed` (around lines 434 and 513).
- `workflow.rs` `assistant_text` and its callers in `workflow.rs` and `graph.rs`.
- `cli/src/repl.rs` (around line 221).
- `runtime-agentcore/src/agui/map.rs` (around lines 366-392).
- `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` `RunResponse::from_events` (they already skip an empty text;
  the guard makes the rule explicit).

The builder searches the workspace for every other consumer of `MessageOutput` or of an
`AssistantMessage` in the item history that takes text, and applies the same guard. The
structured-output path (`loop_state.rs` `last_assistant_content`) runs only on a turn with no tool
calls, so a provider-data-only message cannot reach it. The builder confirms that with a test.

### Core accumulator (`ModelTurnAccumulator`, `build_items`)

- `observe` keeps each `ModelEvent::ProviderData` in arrival order, in a new field.
- `build_items` makes the `AssistantMessage` when text, reasoning **or** provider data is not empty.
  Content order: `Reasoning`, `Text`, then the `ProviderData` parts in arrival order.
- Tool calls stay `Item::ToolCall` items after the message, in the existing `call_id`-sorted order.
- The rustdoc of `ModelTurn::items` changes to say the message can hold provider data only.

### Core: the other places that match on the new variants

- `token_counter.rs` `part_chars`: `ProviderData` counts as 0 characters, because it is not
  model-visible text and only the owning provider sends it. The probe records whether
  `promptTokenCount` changes with the real signature against the dummy. If it changes a lot, the
  builder brings it back before the plan is final.
- `agent.rs` event forwarding (around line 1475): `ModelEvent::ProviderData` is not forwarded as an
  `AgentEvent`. The accumulator still observes it.
- `agent.rs` injection allow-list (around line 1298) already rejects an unknown part. No change.
- The provider-stream conformance suite (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/check.rs`) gets a
  rule: a `ProviderData` with `call_id: Some(id)` names an id of a `ToolCallDelta` in the same
  stream.

### Other provider translators

Each translator already drops an unknown part with a wildcard arm. The changes:

- **OpenAI Chat and LiteLLM.** Today they emit `{"role":"assistant","content":""}` for an
  `AssistantMessage` with only unknown parts. When `Item::ToolCall` items follow, they merge into
  that message, and the result is valid. Alone, it is an empty assistant message. Change: an
  assistant message with no text and no tool calls is not emitted, and the following tool calls
  still form one assistant message. A `UserMessage` with only provider data must not emit
  `{"role":"user","content":[]}`.
- **Bedrock.** Add an explicit silent arm for `ProviderData`, so it does not warn on each request.
- **Anthropic, OpenAI Responses.** They already send nothing for an empty message. Add an explicit
  silent arm where a wildcard would warn.
- **Gemini `user_parts`.** Add an explicit silent arm.

### Gemini stream translator (`sse.rs`, `stream.rs`)

A capture in the repo (`tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs:2225-2274`,
`gemini-3.6-flash`, 2026-08-20) shows: `functionCall.id` is present (`"call_1285087"`),
`thoughtSignature` is a sibling of `functionCall` in the same part (about 700 characters), and the
`STOP` chunk carries `{"text":""}` with no signature. The probe checks this again on 3.8.

- `sse.rs` `Part` gets `thought_signature: Option<String>` (`thoughtSignature` on the wire).
- For each `functionCall` part, the translator emits the `ToolCallDelta`, then
  `ProviderData { provider: "gemini", call_id: Some(<the same call_id>), data }`, where `data` is:

  ```json
  { "index": 0, "thoughtSignature": "<opaque>", "model": "gemini-3.8-flash", "api": "developer" }
  ```

  - `index` is the position of the call among the `functionCall` parts of this response (0, 1, 2,
    …), counted across chunks. It is present on **every** call, signed or not.
  - `thoughtSignature` is present only when the part has one.
  - `model` is the configured model id. `api` is `"developer"` or `"vertex"`. Both are present only
    with a signature.
- The `call_id` is the native id when present. Otherwise it is the existing synthesized
  `fc_<n>`. The request translator sends the same `call_id` as `functionCall.id`, so the pair matches
  in both directions.
- A signature on a part with no `functionCall` is ignored (see the text-level non-goal).
- The key `"gemini"` is exported as a `pub const` of the Gemini crate. The Developer API and Vertex
  share the translator, so they share the key, and `api` tells them apart.

### Gemini request translator (`translate/request.rs`)

**Pairing.** For each `AssistantMessage`, the translator first reads all its Gemini `ProviderData`
parts into a pending list of `(call_id, data)`. Then each `functionCall` (from a `ToolUse` part in
the same message, or from the `Item::ToolCall` items that follow) takes the first pending entry with
the same `call_id` and removes it. The pending list is cleared at the next `AssistantMessage` and at
the next `UserMessage` that is not only tool results. A `ToolResult` does not clear it, because
`close_open_transfers` can put a result between two calls of one response
(`resume_exec.rs:185,194`). The `ProviderData` part itself never becomes a wire part.

Trade-off for damaged histories: if items of two responses with the same call ids interleave with
no `AssistantMessage` between them, a signature can attach to the wrong call. Core never writes that
shape. The result is at worst an HTTP 400 for a history that is already damaged.

**Valid signature.** A signature is valid for this request when `data.model` equals the configured
model id and `data.api` equals the configured transport. A signature that is missing, malformed (not
a string) or not valid is treated as absent. A malformed part never causes an error.

**Order.** In each merged `model` content, when every `functionCall` part has an `index`, the
translator sorts the `functionCall` parts by `index` and keeps the other parts where they are. This
restores the order that Gemini sent. Otherwise the order stays as in the history.

**Signature on the part.** A valid signature goes on the same part:
`{"functionCall": {...}, "thoughtSignature": "..."}`.

**Fallback (dummy signature).** The current turn is every content after the last `user` content
that holds no `functionResponse` part. (SMA-820 shapes 2 and 4: Gemini checks signatures only in that
turn. The tool-result boundary keeps a text in its own content, so a mixed content is not built.) In
the current turn, a `model` content whose `functionCall` parts have no valid signature gets the
documented dummy `skip_thought_signature_validator` on each `functionCall` part. The SMA-820 probe
proved this shape (HTTP 200 on `gemini-3.8-flash`). Outside the current turn, no dummy is added.
This is a hard rule: a content with at least one valid signature is sent as received, and the
other calls stay unsigned, as Gemini returned them. Google says the dummy can make the answer worse,
so it is only the fallback. The dummy goes into one `const` with a doc comment and its source.

**SMA-820 boundary.** The tool-result boundary in `merge_same_role` stays. Its doc comment changes:
the reason is no longer "the SDK sends no signatures". See "Left for Sven".

### Live check (before the Gemini code)

The Google pages that can be reached show no `generateContent` JSON for signatures, so the wire
format comes from live captures. The probe (bash, `curl`, `jq`) runs against the Developer API on
`gemini-3.8-flash`. It reads `GEMINI_API_KEY` from the environment and never prints a header or the
key. Sven runs it, because the agent shell has no key. Captures:

1. A streamed first turn that asks for three parallel calls. Record: where `thoughtSignature` sits,
   which parts carry it, whether `functionCall.id` is present, and whether the signature arrives in
   the same chunk as its call.
2. A streamed text answer: record whether a part carries a signature (information only).
3. Second turn, real signatures as received: expect HTTP 200.
4. Second turn, the signed call moved to the last position: record the result.
5. Second turn, the signed call first and the two unsigned calls swapped: record the result.
6. Second turn, the dummy on each call: expect HTTP 200. Compare `promptTokenCount` with capture 3.
7. Second turn, no signature: expect HTTP 400 (control).
8. SMA-820 shape 3 (`user[functionResponse…, text]` merged) with the real signature: record the
   result, for the boundary decision.
9. When `GEMINI_MODEL_ID_2` is set: capture 3 sent to the second model. Record whether Gemini
   accepts a signature from another model.

The core work and the work in other crates do not depend on the wire shape, so they can start
before the probe results. The Gemini stream and request work waits for the results. If capture 1
shows a different wire shape than this design expects, stop and bring it to Sven. Fixtures are
transcribed from the captures, with each real signature replaced by a placeholder. No real
signature goes into the repo or the PR body. Vertex is not probed; the spec states this limit in the
Gemini README.
